decisions.title: Encore! Encore!
decisions.situation: You bang a spoon on a bowl. It makes a brilliant noise. You would like to check that result another twenty times.

result.title: A short, loud career
result.body: You keep banging until you drop the spoon. You look very pleased with yourself.

journal.text: I discovered how much noise a spoon and a bowl could make.

decisions.title: The two-headed jacket
decisions.situation: You manage to zip two jackets together. They are now one enormous jacket with four sleeves. This may be your greatest invention.

choices.label: Investigate whether a third one would fit
Leave your invention on the floor

result.title: Back to two jackets
result.body: You work out which zip goes where. Both jackets survive the experiment.

journal.text: I worked out how to separate two jackets I had zipped together.

decisions.title: Ready for your close-up
decisions.situation: Anaya points a phone camera at you. You can see yourself on the screen. Your nose deserves further investigation.

choices.label: Move right up to the lens
Wave at the small person on screen
Turn around at the crucial moment

result.title: Mostly nostril
result.body: Anaya keeps the picture. It is a bold choice of composition.

journal.text: I gave Anaya a very close view of my nose.

decisions.title: Missing person: teddy’s eye
decisions.situation: One of your old teddy’s button eyes comes off. You ask Anaya whether teddy needs an ambulance.

choices.label: Stay with teddy until it is fixed

result.title: Outpatient care
result.body: Anaya handles the needle. You choose where the eye belongs.

journal.text: I helped Anaya repair my teddy.

decisions.title: A very close race
decisions.situation: Your shadow keeps reaching the wall before you. You try standing still. It has apparently thought of that too.

choices.label: Make it do a silly dance

result.title: An obedient rival
result.body: You stop trying to beat the shadow and give it increasingly ridiculous instructions.

journal.text: I made my shadow do a silly dance.

decisions.title: The invisible exhibit
decisions.situation: You forgot your show-and-tell. Arjun has already announced that yours is “the best one”. Everyone turns towards your empty hands.

choices.label: Admit you left it at home
Claim it is invisible and dangerous

result.title: A disappointing lack of magic
result.body: Aarav lets you describe it. Arjun whispers that the publicity may have been a mistake.

journal.text: I admitted forgetting my show-and-tell object.

decisions.title: Glitter lockdown
decisions.situation: You spill a pot of glitter during a class project. Aarav finds some inside a closed book.

choices.label: Make a paper funnel for next time

result.title: Still sparkling
result.body: You clean until the bell. There is probably some glitter left in the building forever.

journal.text: I helped clean a classroom after spilling glitter everywhere.

decisions.title: A very short biography
decisions.situation: Arjun passes you a homemade book called “People Who Smell Weird”. Your name is on page one. Every other page is blank.

choices.label: Ask why they made it about you
Write their name on every remaining page

result.title: Needs more characters
result.body: You write “repetitive, poorly researched” on the cover. Arjun laughs, then admits they could not think of a second chapter.

journal.text: I reviewed Arjun’s insulting homemade book as a disappointed critic.

decisions.title: Apparently this was cool
decisions.situation: Anaya plays a song they loved at your age. There is a lengthy explanation of how nobody makes music properly anymore.

choices.label: Ask what it reminds them of

result.title: Before they were your parent
result.body: The story is better than expected. You learn something new about Anaya.

journal.text: I listened to Anaya’s old music and the story behind it.

decisions.title: Answers attached
decisions.situation: Arjun sends you a photo of tomorrow’s homework answers. Their message says “delete after reading”, which sounds very normal.

choices.label: Offer to work through it together
Copy it, including the wrong date

result.title: Less convenient
result.body: You work through the questions. You understand the method by the end.

journal.text: I did my own homework after Arjun sent a photo of the answers.

decisions.title: Your debut single is chemistry
decisions.situation: Arjun secretly records you singing chemistry definitions and adds a dance beat. The file is called “Desperate for Zinc”. They want to send it to the class.

choices.label: Demand credit as the anonymous vocalist
Record a completely unnecessary key change

result.title: An extremely limited release
result.body: Arjun deletes it while you watch. They call you difficult. You call them a record label with no permission forms.

journal.text: I made Arjun delete a secret recording of my chemistry revision song.

decisions.title: Immortal words, wrong person
decisions.situation: The yearbook proof puts Arjun’s quote under your photo: “I peaked at nine.” Priya needs corrections today. You are not sure you want to ask what happened at nine.

choices.label: Return the quote to its rightful owner
Approve it as your mysterious backstory

result.title: A corrected confession
result.body: Priya fixes the names. Arjun explains that they won a particularly good sack race.

journal.text: I corrected swapped yearbook quotations.

decisions.title: Your parent knows this level
decisions.situation: You promise Anaya one last round. They sit down, watch your first attempt and say, “I used to beat this blindfolded.” This is an outrageous development.

choices.label: Agree on one round each, then stop

result.title: Dignity preserved
result.body: You keep your promise and turn it off. Anaya seems more pleased about that than any old high score.

journal.text: I stopped a game when I had promised Anaya I would.

decisions.title: A previous version of you
decisions.situation: Anaya finds an old recording of you explaining how rain works. Your theory involves somebody emptying a bath above the clouds.

choices.label: Ask to keep the recording private

result.title: The expert stands corrected
result.body: You laugh at your explanation. Anaya remembers the questions that came after it.

journal.text: I watched an old childhood recording with Anaya.

decisions.title: Sent to the group
decisions.situation: You send “Whoever made this group is unbearable” to the group itself. The admin replies, “Hi.” You can see several people typing.

choices.label: Admit you meant a different chat

result.title: A successful retreat
result.body: You miss the replies and spend the afternoon doing something else. The message remains embarrassing; you stop watching it happen.

journal.text: I muted a group after sending an insulting message to it.

decisions.title: Water with a personal brand
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, a presenter claims their water has been “emotionally filtered”. The jug beside it is labelled TAP. You are just thirsty.

choices.label: Ask which emotions the filter removes
Debate the emotional lives of liquids

result.title: No emotional processing required
result.body: It tastes like water. The presenter watches you finish a glass with the expression of someone witnessing sabotage.

journal.text: I chose tap water at a premium-water demonstration.

decisions.title: Fun fact about yourself
decisions.situation: You must introduce yourself with one fun fact. The person before you announces they once swallowed a coin. Everyone turns to you expecting escalation.

choices.label: Give your name and disappoint them
Claim you only eat paper money
Recite your entire biography at speed

result.title: No coins were harmed
result.body: You say you like music. A perfectly ordinary fact survives in a room briefly obsessed with swallowing things.

journal.text: I gave a simple introduction after someone set an alarming standard.

decisions.title: You must make the most of it
decisions.situation: You feel better rested than usual and immediately begin planning enough tasks to use every available bit of energy.

choices.label: Choose a few priorities and leave room
Enjoy feeling well without a quota
Fill every bit of the day

result.title: A useful day with an ending
result.body: You use some energy without treating all of it as a resource that must be exhausted.

journal.text: I paced a good day instead of filling every available moment.

decisions.title: The compliment has the wrong address
decisions.situation: Someone praises an anonymous poem you were standing beside at a free exhibition. You did not write it. They are waiting for you to explain its “raw emotional honesty”.

choices.label: Thank them, then admit it is not yours
Point out the actual poet’s name
Accept the praise and invent your inspiration

result.title: A narrow escape from poetry
result.body: They laugh at the mix-up. You both admit you were not entirely sure what the last line meant.

journal.text: I corrected a stranger who thought I had written a poem.

decisions.title: The door does not believe in you
decisions.situation: An automatic shop door refuses to open for you. It opens for a child, a trolley and a blowing receipt. You step forward. Nothing. The cashier points at the sensor and suggests waving.

choices.label: Ask the cashier to let you out

result.title: Assisted departure
result.body: The cashier walks over. The doors open immediately for them. They hold the sensor while you leave, like a bouncer escorting out a ghost.

journal.text: I had to ask a cashier to release me through an automatic door.

decisions.title: A few words from our guest
decisions.situation: At a free local event, the host hands you a microphone and thanks you for “everything you did”. You have no idea what you allegedly did.

choices.label: Ask what you are being thanked for
Thank everyone who made this possible

result.title: The right person is found
result.body: You were mistaken for the person who fixed a blocked toilet. Their arrival receives the applause they earned.

journal.text: I corrected a mistaken public thank-you before giving a speech.

decisions.title: A striking resemblance
decisions.situation: A caricaturist at a street fair in Delhi offers you a free sample portrait. A small crowd gathers. The artist turns the drawing around. It is you as an enormous angry thumb.

choices.label: Ask whether they could add a jawline
Ask for a pencil and draw the artist

result.title: The formal thumb
result.body: The artist adds a bow tie. You point out that this is not a jawline. A spectator says the resemblance is uncanny. You leave holding a thumb in evening wear.

journal.text: I asked a caricaturist to correct my portrait and received a thumb in a bow tie.

decisions.title: The naked gardener
decisions.situation: The community garden in Delhi needs volunteers. Its organiser is wearing a novelty apron printed with a naked torso and refuses to explain it.

choices.label: Ask about the plants, very specifically
Decide you have seen enough nature

result.title: A productive misunderstanding
result.body: You clear a whole bed. Three passers-by stop to stare before realising the torso has pockets.

journal.text: I volunteered beside a gardener in an alarming novelty apron in Delhi.

decisions.title: Practice grief
decisions.situation: At a free estate-planning demonstration, volunteers act as fictional heirs. Your card says “loving relative”. The person beside you is already asking what the imaginary house is worth.

choices.label: Ask how real inheritance rules work
Demand the imaginary house in character

result.title: A family worth inventing
result.body: You deliver a moving line about the fictional deceased. The facilitator thanks you. Your neighbour asks whether the line helped your share.

journal.text: I played a grieving relative at an estate-planning demonstration.

decisions.title: Discreet volunteers wanted
decisions.situation: You post a request for cleanup volunteers in a community chat. Your phone attaches an old shopping list: bleach, bin bags and cable ties. Someone replies, “What exactly are we cleaning?”

choices.label: Explain that it is a garden cleanup

result.title: The photographs help
result.body: You attach a photo of weeds and broken plant pots. Two people volunteer. A third asks for a picture of you holding today’s newspaper. You decline that part.

journal.text: I explained a suspicious shopping list attached to my garden-cleanup request.

decisions.title: You need medical attention
decisions.situation: Your symptoms have become serious: a prolonged low mood and loss of interest. A hospital assessment can begin treatment and may require a short stay. The quoted care costs ₹1,800.00; an unpaid emergency bill remains a real obligation.

result.title: Medical care arranged
result.body: The assessment, treatment outcome and bill are recorded. A hospital stay affects study and paid work as time passes.

journal.text: I accepted urgent medical care.

decisions.title: Honest feedback, preferably positive
decisions.situation: At a free tasting, you try a cracker that tastes strongly of cupboard. The demonstrator asks for a glowing testimonial while holding a camera.

choices.label: Deliver a dramatic account of the cupboard

result.title: A review they can use
result.body: You mention the texture and the cupboard problem. The camera lowers. They admit this batch has been “challenging”.

journal.text: I gave specific criticism of a free food sample.

choices.label: Give it a terrible score for poor eye contact

result.title: A quiet, grounded child
result.body: You praise its composure and excellent leaves. The grower wipes away a tear. A rival arrives with a swaddled turnip and demands equal time.

journal.text: I praised a bonnet-wearing cabbage at a vegetable baby contest.

decisions.title: Happy statistical decline
decisions.situation: For your birthday, someone sends a list of famous people who had achieved more by your age. They finish with “Hope this inspires you!”

choices.label: Choose one goal that is actually yours

result.title: Cake remains an achievement
result.body: You put the list aside. Your day improves immediately when it stops competing with a dead inventor.

journal.text: I ignored an unhelpful achievement list on my birthday.

decisions.title: The lost hand
decisions.situation: You pick up a glove from a bench. A rubber hand slides out of its sleeve. It has painted fingernails, a wristwatch and no obvious owner.

choices.label: Leave it upright on the bench
Ask around for anyone missing a hand

result.title: Please wave if this is yours
result.body: The receptionist holds the hand above the counter. A magician hurries over, thanks you and immediately removes its thumb. You stop watching.

journal.text: I returned a magician’s rubber hand to reception.

decisions.title: The potato has a doctorate
decisions.situation: An acquaintance claims they can cure your Depression. Their method involves a specially trained potato. You ask what training a potato receives. They say that is proprietary.

choices.label: Say you will wait for a peer-reviewed vegetable
Ask to see the potato’s qualifications

result.title: The potato is unavailable for questions
result.body: They offer to remove the sprouts at no extra charge. You end the conversation before discussing the postgraduate options.

journal.text: I declined a supposed potato cure for Depression.

decisions.title: The song of extra garlic
decisions.situation: At a community singalong, the lyric projector fails. It starts displaying a takeaway receipt instead. The backing track continues. Everyone looks to you for the first line.

choices.label: Pass the microphone down the row
Demand that they restore the proper words

result.title: Hold the onions
result.body: You hit the high note on “extra garlic”. The room joins in for “delivery instructions”. The organiser finally switches off the projector during the sauce options.

journal.text: I led a singalong using a takeaway receipt as the lyrics.

decisions.title: It cannot have been this bad
decisions.situation: You revisit a comedy you have called your favourite for years. Ten minutes in, a man falls into a bucket for the fourth time. You appear to have remembered a much better programme.

choices.label: Work out what you used to enjoy
Watch the whole thing out of loyalty

result.title: The bucket loses a fan
result.body: You stop watching without trying to defend your younger self in court. There are other ways to spend the evening.

journal.text: I stopped pretending to enjoy an old favourite programme.

decisions.title: Older than bread
decisions.situation: A birthday cake for you arrives with an extra zero among the candles. Someone asks whether you knew the person who invented bread.

choices.label: Ask for the extra candles to be removed
Keep the cake and accept your ancient status
Deliver a speech about surviving the last ice age

result.title: A breakthrough in reverse ageing
result.body: They remove the extra candles, then stand back as though they have made you younger. You thank the bakery for its medical breakthrough.

journal.text: I corrected an extra zero on my birthday cake.

decisions.title: Reply all
decisions.situation: You meant to send “Is that wig on backwards?” to one person. It lands in the whole public-meeting chat. The wig’s owner is typing.

choices.label: Claim you meant your own wig
Keep reopening the chat in horror

result.title: An honest public disaster
result.body: You admit it was rude. The owner replies, “It is on correctly.” Nobody asks which part you meant to apologise for.

journal.text: I apologised after sending a rude wig comment to a group chat.

Debate the emotional lives of liquids
